units.function: Embedded-Postgres integration suite for Plugin host services that reconcile, resolve, relink and reset Plugin-managed Company Skills using stable resource keys and default-drift reporting.
units.dependencyDirection: Tests enter through buildHostServices with a real database and stubbed event bus, exercising Plugin manifest, Plugin/resource/Skill rows and host service composition. Filesystem, real event delivery, Agent assignment and executable Plugin worker behavior are outside scope.
units.keyDataModels: Plugin manifest ID/API/version/author/capability/worker/Skills; CompanySkill; PluginManagedResource company/kind/key/resource binding; generated canonical Skill key; file inventory; operator-modified content; defaultDrift changedFiles.
units.lifecycle: Install Plugin row; reconcile declared Skill; create canonical CompanySkill and binding; resolve idempotently; preserve operator edits; relink orphaned canonical Skill; report default drift; explicitly reset to manifest defaults; inject canonical key into supplied Markdown.
units.testAssessment: All 281 lines were read once. The 6 tests specify valuable declarative reconciliation behavior: stable ownership keys, no-op timestamps, local-edit preservation, orphan relinking, drift reporting and explicit reset. Focused Vitest was run outside the sandbox, but embedded PostgreSQL failed after five attempts and all 6 tests were skipped, so 0 runtime tests passed. Missing cases cover cross-tenant/key collisions, upgrade/downgrade/uninstall, delete/rename, concurrent reconcile/reset, transaction/event failure, malicious paths/content, executable admission, package authenticity/license and Agent-assignment consequences.
units.designRationale: Let a Plugin declare durable company capabilities that the host can recreate and locate by stable keys without overwriting operator customization unless an explicit reset is requested.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs declarative Connector/Plugin-owned resources with stable opaque ownership, desired-versus-observed drift, tenant isolation, safe upgrade/uninstall, explicit adoption/reset, package provenance, approval and durable reconciliation evidence.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the stable owner/resource key, idempotent reconcile, edit-preserving drift, relink and explicit reset test matrix. Rebuild it on Company OS Plugin/Connector ports with signed/versioned packages, transactional outbox, actor/approval/action digest, upgrade/rollback/uninstall plans and capability/data/egress admission. Do not reuse Paperclip tables or sourceType taxonomy.
units.responsibilityConflict: Plugin capability declaration can create/reset Company Skills without any accountable human, approval or action digest in the tested API. The permission/package publisher is not authenticated, reset attribution is absent, and downstream Agent capability changes are not projected into responsibility evidence.
evidence: 0096b56a1c4e69c077320c0194c804cdaea7615d [codex] Add LLM Wiki plugin host support (#5597)
focused Vitest: 1 file and 6 tests skipped after embedded PostgreSQL failed five times; 0 passed
securityFindings: Manifest author is an unauthenticated string; signature, package digest, publisher identity and license are absent from the fixture.
Plugin-managed Skill declarations have no hashes, trust classification, tool/data/egress scopes or explicit executable admission.
Reset is destructive but has no actor, approval, expected prior digest or immutable receipt.
No cross-company/key collision, concurrency, transaction/event failure, upgrade/downgrade/uninstall or Agent-assignment safety cases are tested.
SourceType catalog conflates Plugin ownership with catalog provenance and can obscure lifecycle authority.
The event bus is a no-op stub, so durable event ordering, replay and failure behavior are unverified.
